subject: Re: IP claim received — proposed resolution & workplan
messages:
From: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice of claimed infringement — request for response

Kimberly,

Attached is a notice we received alleging that outputs generated via your platform for one of our users may have reproduced copyrighted material owned by a third party. We need Redwood's position on coverage and your proposed defense approach under the Master Services Agreement (MSA) and the current order form.

Key asks:
- Confirmation of whether Redwood will defend & indemnify Acme for third-party IP claims tied to model outputs.
- Point of contact for evidence requests and timelines.
- Any immediate mitigation steps you recommend while we triage.

I attached the allegation and the initial takedown demand. Please treat as time-sensitive.

Thanks,
Dana Ruiz
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp
Attachment: Acme_IP_Notice.pdf
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice of claimed infringement — request for response

Dana —

Thanks for sending this over and flagging urgency. We received the PDF and have opened an internal triage. High-level response for now: Redwood is committed to working through third-party claims per our MSA/Order Form but coverage depends on the claim scope and whether the alleged infringement arises from customer-provided content, customer prompts, or model pretraining sources.

Immediate next steps we propose (doable within 24–72 hours):
1) Evidence intake: please use the attached evidence-request template to provide the claimant materials, timestamps, and any example outputs you believe are infringing. This will accelerate our technical review.
2) Technical hold: avoid deleting any customer data or model logs in scope; we may need a limited export.
3) Proposed contact: I will lead legal coordination; Ben (ops) will handle logs/trace, Marissa (CS) will coordinate with your technical team for remediation.

I attached the intake template. We will circulate a proposed workplan once we review the materials.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
Attachment: evidence-request-template.xlsx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal — Acme IP notice (triage + recommended carve)

Kimberly / Ben — quick internal note after reviewing the PDF and sampling the model logs:

Observations:
- The alleged material appears to be a short excerpt (under 300 characters) that matches publicly available content; we see similar n-gram overlap in training traces but not a 1:1 dump.
- Customer seems to have used the platform in a standard way; no evidence yet of prompt injection or exfiltration.

Open legal policy levers I recommend we propose to Acme (to limit exposure while keeping the commercial relationship intact):
1) Narrowed indemnity: accept defense for third-party claims only to the extent the claim arises from Redwood's gross negligence or breach of a specific warranty (rather than broad output-based indemnity).
2) Evidence-driven cooperation: require claimant to produce proof of a verbatim reproduction and allow Redwood to validate against training provenance (to the extent we can).
3) Defense control: ask for joint defense for now — Redwood will participate but request right to appoint counsel for technical defense strategy, with cost-sharing if Acme is pursuing broad statutory damages beyond direct remediation.

I'll draft suggested contract language redlines for the order form (narrow indemnity + evidence gating + limited liability cap applicability).

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success
From: legal-notices@acme-corp.com <legal-notices@acme-corp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: dana.ruiz@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice of claimed infringement — proposed path forward

Kimberly / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the intake template (we returned a completed version attached). Acme's position (short):
- We need Redwood to defend & indemnify Acme for third-party claims that arise from outputs generated while our account is active under the current Order Form.
- We are prepared to be pragmatic on evidence — if Redwood can show a reproducibility report indicating the output is not a verbatim reproduction of the claimant's work, we will pause escalation.
- For defense control: Acme prefers Redwood to accept defense but agrees to a cooperation model where we select jointly agreed counsel for the technical portions; we will not accept carveouts for "gross negligence" as a sole limit.

Proposed compromise items we will accept:
- Redwood takes defense for covered claims, subject to an indemnity cap equal to the order form's liability cap.
- Acme provides claimant evidence and permits Redwood 10 business days for an initial technical validation before escalating.

Attached: completed evidence-request-template.xlsx, and a redline proposal to the order form (minor wording).

Regards,
Acme Legal Notices
Attachments: evidence-request-template.xlsx, acme-orderform-redline.docx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@acme-corp.com>, legal-notices@acme-corp.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 17:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IP claim — agreed operational workplan & next steps

Dana / Acme team — thank you for the completed intake and the pragmatic tone. We are aligned on a stepped approach. Summary of the operational plan we will follow (please confirm by EOD Monday):

1) Intake & hold (completed): Acme provided claimant materials and sample outputs. Do not purge logs for the time being.
2) Technical validation (10 business days): Redwood engineering will run reproducibility checks and provenance scans. Ben will lead and will reach out to Acme's infra lead for temporary access to relevant logs.
3) Legal assessment (concurrent): I will review MSA/order form language and propose two redline options: (A) Redwood indemnifies covered claims and accepts defense subject to the existing liability cap and a joint-counsel cooperation model; (B) if the claimant demonstrates identical verbatim reproduction attributable to Redwood-only sources, Redwood will accept exclusive defense and full indemnity (still within cap).
4) Evidence gating: Acme to produce full claimant evidence within 48 hours; Redwood to notify within 72 hours if further data is required.
5) Escalation: If technical validation is inconclusive after 10 business days, we will move to a mediation call among counsel before any public takedown or litigation.

Attachments and admin: I attached our suggested orderform redline (orderform-redlines-kp-v2.docx) with the two options called out. Laura — can you prepare a short exec note for Sales to explain the customer-facing compromise if they ask? Marissa — please draft the customer communications timeline and confirm who will be the technical touchpoint.

If Acme confirms, we will prepare a DocuSign for the narrow redline amendment and the mutual cooperation statement so we can close this operational loop quickly.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
Attachment: orderform-redlines-kp-v2.docx
